definitions.explanation: An honorific term used when speaking about the listener's company. Used in spoken conversation, especially in job interviews and business meetings.

examples.japanese: {御社|おんしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{事業|じぎょう}→事業：11421_jigyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{興味|きょうみ}→興味：01316_kyoumi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: I am interested in your company's business.

examples.japanese: {御社|おんしゃ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{働|はたら}きたい→働く：00503_hataraku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}い→思う：00492_omou⟧、⟦{応募|おうぼ}→応募：03014_oubo⟧⟦いたしました→いたす：01314_itasu⟧。
examples.english: I applied because I would like to work at your company.

examples.japanese: {御社|おんしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{企業理念|きぎょうりねん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{共感|きょうかん}→共感：09050_kyoukan⟧し、ぜひ⟦{貢献|こうけん}→貢献：02737_kouken⟧⟦したい→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{考|かんが}えて→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧⟦おります→おる：01324_oru⟧。
examples.english: I sympathize with your company's corporate philosophy and would very much like to contribute.

notes:
USAGE:
{御社|おんしゃ} is used in SPOKEN contexts (interviews, meetings, phone calls). For WRITTEN contexts (cover letters, emails, formal documents), use ⟦{貴社|きしゃ}→貴社：15664_kisha⟧ instead. This distinction is important and frequently tested in Japanese business etiquette.

NOTE: Both words are keigo (honorific language) and should only be used to refer to someone else's company, never your own. To refer to your own company humbly, use ⟦{弊社|へいしゃ}→弊社：17404_heisha⟧ (our company, humble).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {御社|おんしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{事業|じぎょう}→事業：11421_jigyou⟧ (your company's business)
- {御社|おんしゃ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧ (to work at your company)
- {御社|おんしゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{応募|おうぼ}→応募：03014_oubo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to apply to your company)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{貴社|きしゃ}→貴社：15664_kisha⟧: your company (written honorific) — used in letters and documents
- ⟦{弊社|へいしゃ}→弊社：17404_heisha⟧: our company (humble) — used when referring to one's own company
